design: MemoryLifecycleCoordinator implements the LLD v1.1 §2.8.1 MemoryLifecycleCoordinator for the closed OpenAPI MemoryLifecycleRequest (transitionMemoryLifecycle) and MemoryDeletionRequest (requestMemoryDeletion) plus two governed jobs, enforce_expiry and enforce_retention. The FSM is exactly ADD v1.3 Part II §2.10 (the test parses the normative block and compares it with TRANSITIONS).

A transition is a new immutable version of the item: the head mapping with memory_version+1, supersedes_ref = head, lifecycle_status = target, created_at = boundary clock, correction_of_ref/legal_hold_ref/prior_lifecycle_status/deletion_epoch reset and re-set only as the target requires; content, provenance and every isolation attribute are unchanged, so the version stays in the item's partition. It is appended to the memory version ledger as one record with its lifecycle event (operation, request digest, from/to, reason, hold, epoch) and its audit event, then committed by the real store coordinator with the predecessor's verified content and the embedding re-derived by the pinned model and checked against embedding_digest; the coordinator retires the predecessor's projections. Retrieval (0052/REM-0020), embedding rebuild (0053) and consolidation (0054) serve only an ACTIVE head, inside the backend query, so exclusion is effective from the commit. Parallel representations of the partition are invalidated by the same transition.

Visibility: the caller sees the item only with the same tenant, organization, domain and purpose, compartments covering the item's and a marking dominating it; otherwise the item is refused exactly like an unknown id. The live LifecyclePolicy decision must be permitted and bound to the context policy bundle. Reason codes are bounded upper-case codes, never free text; DELETION_PENDING needs a forgetting trigger of ADD §2.10. DELETED and DELETION_INCOMPLETE are saga-only. Re-opening (target ACTIVE) reads the stop epoch before and after building the version; exclusions do not depend on the stop state.

Legal hold: LEGAL_HOLD needs a legal_hold_ref that the LegalHoldRegistry reports as an active hold of the item's tenant; the version records legal_hold_ref and prior_lifecycle_status. While the item is LEGAL_HOLD, deletion, forgetting and leaving the hold are refused with LEGAL_HOLD_ACTIVE until the registry reports the hold released; then only the recorded prior disposition or DELETION_PENDING is accepted. The retention sweep reports held items as protected and never touches them.

Deletion saga: the epoch is reserved in the tombstone journal (STARTED; a retry from DELETION_INCOMPLETE reuses its epoch), a content-free DELETION_PENDING version (STRUCTURED only, no embedding fields, deletion_epoch) is committed in the metadata store and the native projections of every earlier version are retired, then every DeletionParticipant purges and re-reads its residue: native lexical/vector entries of every version, parallel embedding descriptors and entries (0053 invalidate), private content objects in every partition of the item (an object referenced by an undeleted item is retained and counted), and any configured cache/replica/export participant. No residue: DELETED version plus COMPLETED tombstone; residue: DELETION_INCOMPLETE version plus INCOMPLETE tombstone with per-participant residue counts and a FAILED receipt. Tombstones carry item id, tenant, partition digests, version refs, epoch, phase, reason, operation, participant names, residue counts and the retained count, never content or content digests.

Sweeps: enforce_expiry transitions every visible ACTIVE head with expires_at at or before the boundary clock to EXPIRED; enforce_retention forgets every visible item whose configured retention horizon elapsed since its first admission. Selection is ordered by due instant then item id; an optional limit defers the rest; each item uses its own idempotent operation id; the job is audited.

LifecycleGuardPolicy wraps the admission policy: a new version is admitted only on a PROPOSED, ACTIVE or QUARANTINED head, so admission cannot re-open a revoked, expired, superseded, held or forgotten item.

Idempotency: each operation_id binds one request digest (operation, item, version, target, reason, hold, GCS digest); a replay returns the recorded receipt and completes an interrupted commit or saga, another request under the same id is MEMORY_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT/OPERATION_REUSED. Every refusal is audited (reason, detail, operation, item id, GCS digest, binding, correlation); an unaudited denial or transition fails closed with AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE and the transition is completed by its replay. Metrics use the bounded label set operation x {COMPLETED, REPLAYED, DENIED, INCOMPLETE} x closed reason code or participant name.

normative_interpretations: ADD v1.3 Part II §2.5 lists the changes that create a new version; lifecycle transitions are represented the same way (new immutable version with the target status), as already anticipated by the OCOR-DEV-0052/0053 test helpers, because the closed GovernedMemoryItem carries lifecycle_status, legal_hold_ref, prior_lifecycle_status and deletion_epoch and the admission service admits only PROPOSED/ACTIVE/QUARANTINED. No contract changes.

The FSM edge LEGAL_HOLD -> DELETION_PENDING coexists with 'Legal hold blocks deletion' (§2.10): it is accepted only after the hold authority reports the hold released (fail-closed reading). LEGAL_HOLD -> prior disposition likewise needs the release. QUARANTINED -> LEGAL_HOLD is not an edge of §2.10 and is refused although the schema's prior_lifecycle_status enum lists QUARANTINED (ADD precedence).

Deletion scope: ALL_VERSIONS is implemented; LATEST_VERSION, PROJECT_SCOPE and PRINCIPAL_SCOPE are refused with UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY (fail closed, no partial deletion). Restore reconciliation from tombstones, caches, replicas, exports and backups beyond the configured participants are OCOR-DEV-0056/0059.

Exclusions (revocation, expiry, hold, quarantine, forgetting) never wait on the stop state: a kill switch cannot keep excluded memory retrievable. Re-opening to ACTIVE requires a readable, unchanged stop epoch.

Retention runs from the first admission of the item (created_at of version 1) under the retention_policy_ref of the head and the configured horizon (ADD §2.13); an unconfigured horizon is reported as unresolved and never deleted. Expiry uses expires_at only; valid_until bounds validity, not existence.

requirement_results.command: FGM-10 on real PostgreSQL 16 (metadata, encrypted content, full-text index, representation descriptors), Qdrant 1.15.1 (native and parallel vector indexes) and OpenBao 2.6.2 transit: a revocation is version n+1 (supersedes_ref = head, same content, lifecycle_status REVOKED) committed through the real 0053 coordinator; version n stays byte-identical; the item leaves STRUCTURED, FULL_TEXT, VECTOR, HYBRID and the parallel v2 representation (descriptor invalidated) while every other hit is unchanged; expiry sweeps select by expires_at then item id, are bounded by a limit (rest deferred), are idempotent and identical on a twin world; REVOKED/EXPIRED never re-open (FSM of ADD v1.3 Part II §2.10 parsed from the normative text and compared exactly); re-opening a QUARANTINED item needs a readable, unchanged stop epoch while an exclusion never waits on the stop state

FGM-10/FGM-16 on the real backends: a world whose strongest matches are held, revoked, superseded or deleted returns exactly the same refs, final scores, score factors and explanation count in every retrieval mode as a twin world that never contained them, and the raw backend query (search_eligible, predicate in the WHERE clause) carries no excluded entry; retrieval keeps no cache and the parallel representation is invalidated; a new version cannot be admitted on an excluded head (LifecycleGuardPolicy); unknown and invisible items (other compartment, purpose or a dominating marking) are refused identically

FGM-11 on the real backends: LEGAL_HOLD records legal_hold_ref and prior_lifecycle_status and needs an active hold of the item's tenant (unknown, foreign or released holds refused); while held, requestMemoryDeletion, a forgetting transition and the retention sweep are refused or report the item as held, and content, native entries and ledger stay unchanged; leaving the hold needs the registry to report it released (outage fails closed) and restores exactly the prior disposition (ACTIVE becomes searchable again, REVOKED stays excluded), or enters deletion

FGM-12 on the real backends: the saga reserves a deletion epoch, commits a content-free DELETION_PENDING version (retrieval closed at once), purges native lexical/vector entries of every version, parallel descriptors and private content objects in every partition of the item (also after reclassification), retains an object still referenced by an undeleted item, re-reads the residue and only then commits DELETED with a durable, hash-chained, content-free tombstone; old exact versions fail closed; a failing replica participant leaves DELETION_INCOMPLETE (FAILED receipt, residue counts, absent from retrieval) until a governed retry under the same epoch completes it; unsupported deletion scopes and non-trigger reasons are refused

FGM-19 on the real backends: the retention sweep forgets items whose configured horizon elapsed since their first admission, ordered by due instant then item id and bounded by a limit, assigns deletion epochs in that order, reports held items as protected and PROPOSED or unconfigured-horizon items as unresolved without deleting them; forgetting triggers and the OpenAPI lifecycle/deletion request shapes are the declared vocabulary

failure injection on the real backends: a store failure after the ledger append and a crash inside the saga after DELETION_PENDING leave the item excluded or unchanged and the replay of the same operation completes it, while another operation is refused (HEAD_NOT_COMMITTED, DELETION_IN_PROGRESS); a lifecycle version whose embedding the pinned model does not reproduce is refused before any write (EMBEDDING_NOT_REPRODUCIBLE); lifecycle state, tombstones and operation ids persist across fresh adapters over the journal ledger; closed envelopes, bounded reason codes, deadline, GCS binding, stale versions, policy denial/outage/stale bundle are refused before any write; every refusal is an audited denial and an unaudited denial or transition fails closed; metrics are bounded; the module has no backend client and no authority path

residual_risks: Item metadata of every version (including content digests) stays in the hash-chained version ledger and in metadata after deletion; content, projections and representations are purged and the tombstone is content-free. Membership inference on low-entropy content through retained digests is a residual risk for OCOR-DEV-0056/0059 (metadata minimisation and backup/restore).

A failure between the ledger append and the store commit leaves the previous head served until the replay of the same operation; the caller receives the failure. Exclusion is effective from the commit.
LifecycleGuardPolicy protects admission only where it is composed into the admission policy chain (as in the tests); production wiring is outside this task.
The PostgreSQL/Qdrant/OpenBao adapters are the 0051/0053 test adapters; no production adapter under memory/adapters/ exists yet.

Test-level anonymous Docker volume leaks in pre-existing suites remain allocated to OCOR-DEV-REM-0018 (see the full-suite resource attribution); the 0055 task suite itself leaves no container, volume or network (task-teardown-delta).

tdd.REFACTOR: First live run exposed two wrong test oracles (the fixture evidence of 0051 is retained 30 days, so the young item of the retention case is admitted 20 days later; an operation id reused by a fresh world is correctly refused as OPERATION_REUSED, now asserted). A preliminary mutation probe (51 mutants) left nine survivors: one was a redundant check and was removed (the replay visibility check: the request digest already binds the caller's GCS); one exposed an ordering defect, fixed (the predecessor content and the re-derived embedding are now read and verified before the ledger append, so a non-reproducible embedding writes nothing); seven exposed missing tests, now added (a complete but unacknowledged journal line, a self-consistent entry chained to a wrong predecessor, other tenant/organization/domain callers, a non-reproducible embedding, raw index exclusion of a pending deletion before any purge, retention anchored at the first admission of a later-revised item, purge of shared content once its last referencing item is deleted, the expiry sweep's own audit event); sweeps now also re-check the FSM edge of every selected head (a revoked item with an elapsed expires_at is never expired). A second probe on the corrected code (50 mutants) left one survivor, the ACTIVE filter of the expiry due-date, made equivalent in outcome by the new FSM re-check except for the report: the expiry case now asserts that a non-ACTIVE head is neither processed nor reported. The final probe kills all 50 mutants.
